newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Jan 6.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - Jan 6.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors affecting Indian stock markets on Monday morning:
NEWS OUTLOOK:
** Indian stocks seen extending rally this week as the trade awaits a promised policy package by the government later this month
"It is apparent that the government is really concerned
about the state of the markets...sentiments have changed," said Ajit Ambani, member-broker of the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE).
A blistering rally by blue-chips on New Year's Day

pushed up the benchmark Bombay stocks index nearly six percent after the government said it would announce in mid-January a policy package to boost industrial growth and revive sagging capital markets

** Government-enforced cuts in cash reserves held by Indian banks, effective from Saturday, seen boosting liquidity and money market conditions but unlikely to cause a substantial rise in credit use, bankers and analysts say
** India's year-on-year inflation rate measured by the wholesale price index rose to 7.58 percent in the week ending December 21 from 7.08 percent in the previous week, the Industry Ministry said

** The Indian government is studying the possibility of making the rupee fully convertible, but the move would have to await an increase in foreign exchange reserves, Commerce Minister Bolla Buli Ramaiah was quoted on Monday as saying
The Press Trust of India quoted Ramaiah as telling a
conference in the southern city of Hyderabad on Sunday that the government would take a decision soon on whether to make the rupee fully convertible on capital account
"We are seriously thinking on how soon we should go in
for full converibility," Ramaiah was quoted as saying. "Once foreign exchange reserves improve further, it will be done."
** The Economic Times says the finance ministry has rejected the proposed $150 million Euro-issue of cash-strapped Shaw Wallace and Co
** Indian exports likely to touch $35 billion, Commerce Minister Bolla Buli Ramaiah quoted as saying in The Economic Times
** The selection of co-managers of the Euro-issue of
Videsh Sanchar Nigam Ltd (VSNL) begins on Monday, according to newspaper reports
It said 21 foreign institutional investors have been
shortlisted
MARKETS:
** Bombay bourse's benchmark index ends 38.76 points or 1.20 pct up at 3264.0 on Friday. National Stock Exchange index up 4.60 points to 931.65
Delhi index rises 4.54 points to 709.39, Calcutta gains
2.45 points to 427.31 and Madras 18.27 points to 3,175.88
** Indian rupee opens steady at 35.89/91 against the dollar on Monday, dealers say
-- Bombay newsroom +91-22-265 9000
